1b8t1fy:253: The most important contribution of LingBot-Vision is not performance improvement, but proposing a "spatially native" visual representation paradigm—centered on geometric structure rather than semantic classification. Traditional visual foundation models (DINOv3, CLIP) use random masking strategies in masked modeling; the model learns the semantic category of an object ("this is a chair") rather than its geometric structure ("this is a three-dimensional structure with four legs and a backrest"). LingBot-Vision actively masks boundary regions, forcing the model to understand the functional partitions and 3D geometric relationships on both sides of object boundaries. This paradigm shift means downstream tasks no longer need to "decode" spatial information from semantic representations—spatial information is encoded in the representation from the start.

qxz0sf:208: Boundary masking faces a chicken-and-egg problem: the model initially does not know where boundaries are, yet boundary masking depends on boundary prediction. The Ant Lingbo team's solution has two steps: First, given sparse corner points, even if the boundary field is initially random, the decoded line segments remain coherent and plausible—"the boundary structure is held up by roughly guessed corner points." Second, introducing an a-contrario test converts boundary prediction into a classification problem, automatically filtering out false boundaries with insufficient significance and preventing training signals from being drowned in noise. This "coarse-to-fine" bootstrapping strategy avoids training collapse and is the key engineering innovation that makes boundary masking actually work.
